# `fluxsim verify`

Re-check an applied run on five independent legs: the run's own artifacts against its recorded digest, the golden regression, row conformance against the referenced contract, the RFC-04 enforcement vectors, and every declared fidelity check. One line per leg, with the flag that turns a `not checked` leg into a result.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim verify [options] <bundle>
```

## Examples

```bash
# re-check an applied run on five independent legs
fluxsim verify ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run-id` | `RUN_ID` | the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`) **(required)** |
| `--update-golden` |  | record this run as the golden baseline (requires --reason) |
| `--reason` | `REASON` | why the golden baseline is being updated |
| `--committed-slice` | `EXPOSE_ID=file://PATH` | the committed real-data slice one expose's fidelity check is measured against, as EXPOSE_ID=file://PATH; repeatable, once per expose; the file holds one JSON object per line, keyed by the expose's contract column names (e.g. {"subscriber_id": "s-1", "amount": "12.50"}) |
| `--vectors` | `VECTORS` | path to an RFC-04 vectors file |
| `--allow-declared-baseline-drift` |  | exit 0 even when the bundle's declared golden.baselineDigest does not match this run's runDigest |
| `--signing-key` | `SIGNING_KEY` | file holding the 32-byte ed25519 seed a prior `fluxsim ship` signed with; its public half becomes the trust anchor, and the check says it is self-attested |
| `--trust-key` | `PATH` | file holding the 32-byte raw ed25519 PUBLIC key (raw or hex -- the `publicKey` a fidelity record prints) any fidelity record this run already holds is checked against; without it, and without --signing-key, the signature is reported as not checked |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
